subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Thévenin's Theorem: Simplify Any Circuit
description: A quick, practical guide to Thévenin's Theorem: Simplify Any Circuit.

hook.text: A circuit with 20 resistors and 5 sources can be reduced to one voltage and one resistor.

buildup.text: Thévenin says any linear network can be replaced by a single source and series resistor.

discovery.text: Find the open-circuit voltage and the equivalent resistance seen from two terminals.

twist.text: Norton's theorem does the same with a current source and parallel resistor instead.

climax.text: Engineers use Thévenin to analyze complex circuits one section at a time.

punchline.text: Any circuit, two terminals, one equivalent — that's Thévenin.

quiz.question: What does Thévenin's theorem produce?
options: A set of differential equations for the circuit
An equivalent circuit with one voltage source and one series resistor
A frequency response plot for the circuit
